{"id": "0681b4d7-7031-48d6-9a1f-75e0d6f662a1", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_fZMLbpla38LCjLmfOnl5MH", "content": "[{'text': '## Documentation search results\\n\\n{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"rank_order\":1,\"title\":\"Export and visualize carbon emissions data from your AWS accounts | AWS Cloud Financial Management\",\"context\":\"## Calculate aggregates by AWS Organization, Regions, and Service\\\\n\\\\nIf you\u2019re signed in as a management account of AWS Organizations, the Customer Carbon Footprint Tool dashboard reports the consolidated member account data. If you\u2019re logged in to a member account, the Customer Carbon Footprint Tool reports emission data only for this account.\\\\n\\\\nUnlike the CCFT console experience, the carbon emissions Data Export always provides individual account-level emissions data, regardless if it\u2019s a payer or member account. If you want to calculate aggregates by AWS Organization, Region, or Product, start with the following query in the Athena query editor:\\\\n\\\\n```\\\\nSELECT\\\\n carbon_model_version,\\\\n model_version,\\\\n usage_period,\\\\n usage_period_start,\\\\n usage_period_end,\\\\n SUM(total_mbm_emissions_value) AS total_mbm_emissions_value,\\\\n total_mbm_emissions_unit,\\\\n payer_account_id,\\\\n product_code,\\\\n region_code,\\\\n location\\\\nFROM <database>.`carbon`\\\\nGROUP BY\\\\n carbon_model_version,\\\\n model_version,\\\\n usage_period,\\\\n usage_period_start,\\\\n usage_period_end,\\\\n total_mbm_emissions_unit,\\\\n payer_account_id,\\\\n product_code,\\\\n region_code,\\\\n location\\\\n\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nIf you want to aggregate by AWS Organization, remove the `product_code`, `region_code` and `location` from the `SELECT` and the `GROUP BY` parts of the SQL statement. Likewise, if you want to aggregate by AWS region, remove the `payer_account_id`, and the `product_code`. Leave only product_code, if you want to get the emissions by service.\\\\n\\\\nIf you want to reuse this query, you can create a **view**, which is a virtual table that saves your query logic for reuse, by running:\\\\n\\\\n`CREATE [ OR REPLACE ] VIEW <database>.<view_name> AS <select query above>`\",\"url\":\"https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws-cloud-financial-management/export-and-visualize-carbon-emissions-data-from-your-aws-accounts/\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"Carbon emissions\",\"context\":\"## Permissions\\\\n\\\\nTo access carbon footprint data, you\\\\nneed the IAM permission\\\\n`sustainability:GetCarbonFootprintSummary`\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cur/latest/userguide/table-dictionary-carbon-emissions.html\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"Updated Carbon Methodology for the AWS Customer Carbon Footprint Tool | AWS Cloud Financial Management\",\"context\":\"## Today\u2019s CCFT update in detail\\\\n\\\\n1. *Making it easier to access data*\\\\n\\\\nTo make it easier to use the data from the CCFT, customers can now export their January data through AWS\u2019s Billing and Cost Management Data Exports service. The carbon emissions data export delivers carbon emissions estimates for all the member accounts linked to their management account, when customers use AWS Organizations. The Data Exports service automatically delivers monthly updates in CSV or Parquet format to Amazon S3, allowing customers to automate the processing of carbon data across their entire AWS organization. With our customers\u2019 first export, they will receive up to 38 months of historical data in their S3 bucket to allow for historical analysis. The data for December 2024 and earlier will be calculated using methodology version 1.0, while January 2025 onwards will use version 2.0. Customers can learn more about how to set up a Data Export in the Data Exports user guide.\\\\n\\\\n2. *AWS Regional Granularity*\\\\n\\\\nCustomers can now see their carbon emissions broken down by AWS Region (ex: US East (Ohio)), with Amazon CloudFront CDN usage broken out as well (represented as a single Global Services category). This means customers can identify the Regions where their usage contributes the most to their carbon footprint to help them re-assess the regional distribution of their workloads on AWS.\\\\n\\\\n3. *The updated v2.0 methodology*\\\\n\\\\nCustomers often use a wide array of AWS services across multiple regions and as a result, tracking and apportioning carbon emissions based on workloads can be challenging. While there is no industry standard for allocating carbon emissions for cloud usage to customers, the update to the v2.0 methodology leveraged existing standards to support the CCFT, including: GHG Protocol Corporate Standard, GHG Protocol Product Standard, ISO 14040/44 (LCA), ISO 14067 (Carbon footprint of products) and ICT Sector Guidance.\\\\n\\\\nCustomers can read more in the full-length methodology document, but here is a brief overview of the approach:\\\\n\\\\nScope 1 Emissions (Direct) Overview for v2.0\\\\n\\\\nScope 1 includes direct emissions from sources owned or controlled by AWS, such as fuel combustion in backup generators at our data centers. AWS receives Scope 1 activity data for the prior year in the first quarter of the following calendar year, as a result of our Amazon-wide annual assurance process. Then, we calculate estimated carbon data with site-level granularity and aggregate it\\\\n\\\\n*[truncated \u2014 additional content omitted]*\",\"url\":\"https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws-cloud-financial-management/updated-carbon-methodology-for-the-aws-customer-carbon-footprint-tool/\"}]}}\\n\\n## Recent AWS announcements (What\\'s New)\\n\\nNewer than your training data may be. When these conflict with the documentation results above or with what you remember, prefer the most recent dated source.\\n\\n{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"rank_order\":1,\"title\":\"Customer Carbon Footprint Tool has new features and an updated methodology - AWS\",\"context\":\"AWS has announced updates to the Customer Carbon Footprint Tool (CCFT), which includes easier access to carbon emissions data, visibility into emissions by AWS Region, and an updated methodology (v2.0). The new feature allows users to export monthly data through AWS\\'s Billing and Cost Management Data Exports service, providing carbon emissions estimates for all member accounts linked to their management account in AWS Organizations\",\"url\":\"https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2025/04/customer-carbon-footprint-tool-updated-methodology/\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"AWS reduces publishing time for Carbon Footprint Data to 21 days or Less - AWS\",\"context\":\"AWS has significantly reduced the publishing time for carbon footprint data from up to three months to 21 days or less. The update provides visibility into the lifecycle carbon impact of AWS usage, including emissions from manufacturing servers, powering AWS facilities, and transporting equipment to data centers. Historical data is available from January 2022, enabling organizations to track their progress and make informed decisions about their cloud strategy to meet sustainability goals. The updated CCFT data is accessible through the dashboard and AWS Billing and Cost Management Data Exports, allowing for easy integration into operational workflows, sustainability planning, and reporting processes. For more information, visit the AWS Billing and Cost Management console or read the updated methodology documentation and release notes\",\"url\":\"https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2025/10/aws-customer-carbon-footprint-tool-scope-3-emissions-data/\"},{\"rank_order\":4,\"title\":\"querying-aws-s3\",\"skill_description\":\"Queries S3 object metadata, tracks bucket activity, audits object changes, searches annotations, and analyzes storage metrics using S3 Metadata system tables (journal, inventory, annotation) and S3 Storage Lens tables via Athena SQL. {"id": "990eec59-0967-4747-958e-4bf95e49c6c3", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "tool_summary", "content": [{"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "tooluse_edmSn8um8T8nG5dLWcYXK3", "status": "success", "content": [{"text": "{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"status\":\"SUCCESS\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cur/latest/userguide/table-dictionary-carbon-emissions.html\",\"content\":\"# Carbon emissions\\n\\nThe carbon emissions table contains your estimated carbon emissions. It provides detailed\\naccount-level and regional granularity of your carbon emissions data. You can configure\\nautomated monthly deliveries to Amazon S3 in either CSV or Parquet format, making it\\nsimple to integrate with your existing business intelligence tools and reporting\\nsystems. For detailed information about the methodology, see Calculation Methodology in the *AWS Sustainability User Guide*.\\n\\nThe SQL table name for carbon emissions is `CARBON_EMISSIONS`.\\n\\n## Historical data\\n\\nYou will receive data going back up to January 2022 within 24 hours of setup, enabling you\\nto perform baseline analysis and trend reporting without manual data\\ngathering.\\n\\n## Table configurations\\n\\nThere are no table configurations for the Carbon emissions table.\\n\\n## Permissions\\n\\nTo access carbon footprint data, you\\nneed the IAM permission\\n`sustainability:GetCarbonFootprintSummary`.\\n\\n## Model versions\\n\\nThe methodology for calculating your carbon emissions will evolve over time to better\\nreflect your usage and align with carbon accounting best practices. Exports are\\npartitioned in hierarchical order by \u201cmodel_version=Y/\u201d and \u201cusage_period=YYYY-MM/\u201d.\\nThe \u201cmodel_version\u201d partition that an export is stored under will correspond to the\\nmodel version used to generate that export, while the \u201cusage_period\u201d partition\\ncorresponds to the dates the carbon emissions were generated. This structure enables\\nyou to differentiate between data with the old and new models by viewing the\\npartition names.\\n\\n## AWS Organizations support\\n\\nThe Carbon emissions table inherits the settings you made in the consolidated\\nbilling feature in AWS Organizations. When consolidated billing is enabled, there\\nare different behaviors for management and member accounts. If you\u2019re using a\\nmanagement account, your Carbon emissions table includes estimated carbon emissions\\ndata for the management account and all member accounts in your organization. If\\nyou\u2019re using a member account, your Carbon emissions table only includes estimated\\ncarbon emissions data for that member account.\\n\\nAfter a member account joins a new organization, or a management account converts to a\\nmember account and joins a new organization, the account's carbon emissions data is\\nrecorded in the new organization's exports. Each management account contains member\\naccounts' data for the time period it was linked to said management account. For\\nexample, a member account leaves organization A and joins organization B on the 15th\\nof the month. Then, the member account creates an export. Because the member account\\ncreated an export after joining organization B, the member account\u2019s export of the\\nCarbon emissions table for the month includes estimated carbon emissions data for\\nthe time that the account has been a member of organization B.\\n\\nWhen a member account leaves an organization or converts to a standalone account, the\\nmember account can still access previous exports if it has permissions to the Amazon\\nS3 bucket where those exports are stored. Carbon emissions associated with\\nterminated or suspended accounts will appear in the management account data exports\\nfor the periods when these accounts were active.\\n\\nFor more information, see Consolidated billing for AWS Organizations in the\\n*AWS Billing User Guide*.\",\"total_length\":3353,\"start_index\":0,\"end_index\":3353,\"truncated\":false,\"redirected_url\":null,\"error_code\":null}]}}"}]}], "label": "Check AWS docs for GetCarbonFootprintSummary API GroupBy dimension values and granularity"}

**API call**

Use the Sustainability service's `GetEstimatedCarbonEmissions` operation (boto3 client `sustainability`, permission `sustainability:GetEstimatedCarbonEmissions`):

```
GroupBy=['USAGE_ACCOUNT_ID', 'SERVICE']
TimePeriod={'Start': '2025-11-01T00:00:00Z', 'End': '2026-11-10T00:00:00Z'}
Granularity='MONTHLY'
EmissionsTypes=['TOTAL_MBM_CARBON_EMISSIONS']   # or LBM / scope-specific types
```

Grouping by both `USAGE_ACCOUNT_ID` and `SERVICE` in one call gets you rows broken out by account‑and‑service combination; if you want a cleaner account‑only and service‑only view, run it twice with a single GroupBy dimension each.

**What shows up as "service" lines**

Each AWS product/service your org actually used gets its own line — e.g. Amazon EC2, Amazon S3, Amazon RDS, AWS Lambda, Amazon CloudFront (broken out as a "Global Services" line rather than tied to a region), etc. Only services with non‑zero allocated emissions appear.

**Granularity and availability — this is the part that'll bite you**

- Finest grain available is **MONTHLY** (also QUARTERLY/YEARLY) — there's no daily or partial-month granularity, so "this month so far" (November) isn't something the tool can produce at all right now.
- AWS publishes each month's emissions data **21 days or less** after month-end, typically landing between the **15th–21st of the following month**.
- Since today is **Nov 10, 2026**: October 2026 hasn't been published yet (expect it ~Nov 15–21), and November won't be available until mid‑December. So your most recent fully available month right now is **September 2026**.
- Practically, a "last 12 months" request today returns complete monthly data from roughly **October 2025 through September 2026** — 12 months, just shifted back by the ~1.5 month publication lag, with October and November 2026 absent.

**What a member account would see running the same call**

A member account's `GetEstimatedCarbonEmissions` call only ever returns that account's own emissions — grouping by `USAGE_ACCOUNT_ID` would just yield their own account ID as the single line, with no visibility into sibling accounts. The consolidated, multi-account view is only available to the Organizations management account (or a delegated admin, if configured).

If you need true "current/this-month" tracking, that's not something the Carbon Footprint API can give you — it's inherently a lagging-indicator tool. Happy to help you pull the actual September-and-earlier numbers once you're ready to run it.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
